findings.evidence: `FiniteTypeTrivial.lean` only declares `trivial`, `trivial_obj`, `trivialIsInitial`, and `eq_unit` (lines 47, 53, 63, 74); the raw one-point equivalence is only `TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv` in `Trivial.lean:52`, while the parallel finite-type product wrapper exposes `pointsMulEquiv` and simp/naturality lemmas in `FiniteTypeProduct.lean:74-146`.
findings.fix: Add a named finite-type trivial points equivalence, e.g. `trivialPointsMulEquiv`, plus `@[simp]` apply/symm and naturality lemmas analogous to `TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv_apply`, `pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply`, and `pointsMulEquiv_mapValue`.
findings.issue: `FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.trivial` has no finite-type points API identifying `(pointsFunctor.obj (op (trivial R))).obj A` with `PUnit`, so consumers of the roadmap's three-way dictionary must unfold `trivial`/`pointsFunctor` and manually reuse the raw `TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv`.

summary: The finite-type trivial object is exposed with its initiality API, but its functor-of-points characterization is missing from the finite-type surface.
